newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cousteau, insurers sue shipyard where Calypso sank.
newsitem.headline: Cousteau, insurers sue shipyard where Calypso sank.

text.p: Ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau and his insurers are suing the Singapore shipyard where the Frenchman's research vessel Calypso sank last year, officials at the Cousteau Society's Paris office said.
Lawyers representing the Cousteau Society in Singapore recently filed a suit seeking compensation for the cash the eight insurers paid out after the Calypso sank in January 1996, they said.
The vessel played a starring role in a long-running television series which pioneered interest in the world's oceans and the conservation of marine life.
The Calypso, in which the 86-year-old French oceanographer had toured the globe since 1950, went down in about five metres (16 feet) of water at the shipyard where it had been berthed.
"This is a simple, routine dispute," one official said, confirming a report on Singapore television. He declined to give any details.
A drifting barge smashed the hull of the Calypso, a 20-metre (66-foot) converted British minesweeper, when it was docked in Singapore before a planned trip to the South China Sea.
The Calypso was salvaged for repairs at a Singapore shipyard. Cousteau last year appealed for donations to build a new $20 million exploration ship, Calypso II.
